newsitem.title: USA: Destec, partners to sell Tiger Bay plant.
newsitem.headline: Destec, partners to sell Tiger Bay plant.

text.p: Destec Energy Inc said on Thursday the Tiger Bay Limited partnership in which it has a 50 percent equity stake signed a deal to sell the 220 megawatt Tiger Bay cogeneration facility for $445 million.

The buyer is a subsidiary of Florida Progress Corp, which said buying the facility is expected to result in customer savings in the range of more than $2 billion over the life of the existing contract that runs to 2025.
Destec estimated its share of the proceeds after repayment of partnership debt and other project obligations at $140 million.
The other Tiger Bay partners are Energy Investors Fund and General Peat.

The plant, which uses an advanced gas-fired combined cycle technology, began commercial operation in January 1995. When it is added to Florida Power's fleet, it will be the most efficient generating unit on the company's system.

Florida Power said it became obligated in the 1980s to sign long-term purchase power contracts with non-utility power producers, such as Tiger Bay, to comply with the 1978 Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act.

But in recent years, generating costs have fallen with the price of natural gas, construction costs and more efficient power plant technology. By buying the plant the company can terminate a now-unfavorable contract.
"By acquiring Tiger Bay, we can take advantage of a unique opportunity that should result in substantial savings," said Joe Richardson, Florida Power president and chief operating officer.

The sale is subject to regulatory approvals and the closing of a potential sale of Destec. The company in October said it retained advisors to explore strategic alternatives, including a possible sale of the company. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
